examples.pie: sérpeti h₁ógʷʰis h₂ḱméni Hn̥dʰí dʰrówgʰos sweh₂dúsu wékʷesu Hn̥dʰí sérpeti. h₂éḱmonm̥ tl̥nh₂dʰí h₁ógʷʰim-kʷe winédsi.
examples.en: The snake creeps under a stone; the lie creeps under sweet words. Lift the stone, and you find the snake.

examples.pie: dyéw nos ph₂ter dʰéǵʰom méh₂ter-kʷe ḱlutóm. dyéw upér tn̥néwsi dʰéǵʰom Hn̥dʰí ḱéyth₂er. dyéw h₂wérs dʰéǵʰom wédos péh₃s h₂orkéyetom nos.
examples.en: Father Sky and Mother Earth, hear us, you two! Sky, you stretch above; Earth, you lie below. Sky, you rained; Earth, you drank the water. Guard us, you two.

examples.pie: tr̥syóh₂ sóh₂wl̥-kʷe dʰégʷʰeti. péh₃tlōd moy ph₃dʰí. wódr̥ póntoh₁i h₁ésti? bʰréh₁wr̥ méǵh₂i dréwi Hn̥dʰí h₁ésti. h₁ésyo sḱh₃yéh₂i kʷih₁dʰí.
examples.en: I am thirsty, and the sun is burning. Drink from my cup. Is there water on the way? There is a spring under the big tree. Rest in its shade.

examples.pie: h₂éwis bʰerHǵóy sédt wĺ̥kʷom-kʷe spéḱyet.
examples.en: The bird sat down in the birch and kept looking at the wolf.

examples.pie: tétḱon moy téntlom ḱl̥nitór. téntlom toy démi bʰerHǵṓd stoh₂éyōh₂. h₃reǵtóm sth₂éh₁yēti? h₃reǵtóm sth₂éh₁yēti. kʷíd h₁ésmi téksesi? suHnówōm moy wésmn̥h₂. nu moy wésmn̥ éti tksdʰí misdʰóm-kʷe ne h₁áyoh₂er. mówdoh₁.
examples.en: Carpenter, my loom leans. I will set up a loom of birch in your house. Will it stand straight? It will stand straight. What will you weave on it? My sons' garments. Then weave me one too, and I will take no wage. With joy!

examples.pie: kʷíh₁ h₁ludʰés? deywṓs h₁mé h₂léksont ḱwṓ-kʷe h₁mé wédʰet. ǵʰwērés bʰéwgm̥ nésm̥-kʷe.
examples.en: "How did you come?" "The gods protected me, and the dog led me. I fled from the beast and returned home unharmed."

examples.pie: kʷíd kʷéḱs? méǵh₂m̥ h₁ógʷʰim widóm. h₁ógʷʰis kʷór ḱéyo? déh₂newi ḱéyo. bʰéwgs? bʰéwgm̥.
examples.en: "What did you see?" "I saw a great snake." "Where was the snake lying?" "It was lying by the river." "Did you flee?" "I fled."

examples.pie: pĺ̥th₂ew tń̥tle ǵʰwḗrm̥ lm̥bʰdʰí h₁ím kapyé. twéd kʷid mē bʰugyéh₁t tn̥tlós-kʷe pl̥nh₁ih₁tó.
examples.en: Broad net, seize the beast, hold it! May nothing flee from you, and may the net become full.

examples.pie: ḱóymosyo pótis h₁léwdʰins dʰoréyeti.
examples.en: The master of the household maintains the people.

examples.pie: h₁eǵóh₂ poh₂imḗn dʰéh₁s-kʷe te sepelyóh₂. h₂óweyes déh₂nus píph₃onti. h₂éngʷʰis-ge déh₂nu dʰoréyet túH h₁íd sélǵs. nu moy téwh₂se h₂ówins wĺ̥kʷōd h₂lékse. nu toy sweh₂dú h₂mélǵos déh₃oh₂.
examples.en: I am a shepherd, and I praise you, god. The sheep drink from the river. A snake indeed held the river; you set it free. Now guard my sheep, strong one, from the wolf! I shall now give you sweet milk.

examples.pie: h₁yód néḱus péh₂urom h₃órbʰom léykʷeti h₁widʰéwh₂ misdʰóm dʰoréyetu. h₁yód h₁éy h₂wékseti só h₂réh₁dʰetu. h₁yód h₁widʰéwh₂ kʷoynéh₂m ne h₁áyetor h₁íh₂m̥ kʷis mē térgʷet. ḱéh₂dos ne wósn̥.
examples.en: If a dead man leaves a small orphan, let the widow hold the payment. When he has grown up, let him decide. If the widow does not take the price, let no one threaten her. Grief is not a trade.

pie-lex-ghrbneh2ti.gloss: to be seizing, grabbing; to be digging

root.gloss: to seize, grab; to dig, rake

examples.pie: ḱḗr mē tréms deywós te péh₂sti. kʷsép l̥gʰdʰí h₂éwsōs h₁ludʰḗti ḱḗr Hwr̥dʰdʰí.
examples.en: Heart, do not tremble. A god protects you. Night, lie down. Dawn will come. Heart, become strong.

examples.pie: h₁yós h₁ludʰḗti só sédeti h₁yós-kʷe linékʷti só stéh₂eti.
examples.en: Whoever arrives shall sit down, and whoever leaves shall stand up.

examples.pie: h₁ludʰḗti gʰóstis só sodéyētor wódr̥-kʷe tósmey déh₃etor.
examples.en: If a guest arrives, he shall be seated and water shall be given to him.

examples.pie: swésōr pr̥téwi sédt udréh₂-kʷe bʰr̥h₁wéns h₁nédʰt.
examples.en: The sister sat down at the crossing, and the aquatic one came forth from the spring.

examples.pie: bʰeh₂nós ḱleytéh₂m skélHt h₁nédʰt-kʷe h₂ékʷeh₂.
examples.en: The shiny one split the slope, and the water came forth.

examples.pie: tósyo h₃bʰrúHs dʰégʷʰet ḱéh₂dos-kʷe h₁nédʰt.
examples.en: His eyebrow burned, and hatred came forth.

examples.pie: kʷís wédesi gʷih₃wós h₁ésti péysks gʷih₃wós h₁ésti.
examples.en: Who is alive in the water? The fish is alive.

examples.pie: kʷís péyskm̥ mréy widéh₁yeti h₃érō tóm widéh₁yeti.
examples.en: Who sees the fish in the sea? The eagle sees it.

examples.pie: kʷíd skʷálos? skʷálos méǵh₂s péysks. h₂ékʷeh₂i tḱéyti dʰǵʰúHn̥s-kʷe gʷr̥h₃éti. mórtōs skʷálom h₁édn̥ti? h₁ím h₁édn̥ti h₁ésyo-kʷe mḗms gʷr̥nHénti.
examples.en: What is a sheatfish? A sheatfish is a big fish. It lives in the water, and it swallows fish. Do people eat the sheatfish? They eat it, and they praise its meat.

root.gloss: to walk, to step; to stumble, to fall

examples.pie: tóm títr̥h₂n̥tu tóm udʰh₁éntu tóm-kʷe swóysu pedsú dʰh₁éntu.
examples.en: Let them overcome him, let them thrust at him, and let them put him at their own feet.

examples.pie: h₁sónt ḱuh₁róm ne-kʷe mért dʰrówgʰos ml̥dús. h₁yós dʰrugʰyéti só bʰéh₂esos bʰebʰóyh₂e. dʰrówgʰosyo pódh₁e mr̥ǵʰúh₁.
examples.en: The truth is strong, and it does not die; the lie is weak. He who deceives fears the light. The feet of a lie are short.

examples.pie: ḱḗr polh₁úh₂ wéḱti ménos péh₂ureh₂ wélh₁t. h₁yósyo ménos h₃reǵtóm só h₃reǵtóy stóygʰoy stéygʰeti. h₁ésyo pódh₁e ne h₃slidʰtā́m.
examples.en: The heart wants many things; the mind chooses few. He whose mind is straight walks on a straight path. His feet do not slip.

examples.pie: nu wódr̥ h₂éǵroysu léyHm̥. pérkʷune h₂éǵroysu h₂wr̥sdʰí. déh₂nuh₂ sréwoyh₁t ǵr̥h₂nóm h₂uksyéh₁t.
examples.en: Now I have poured water on the fields. Perkunos, rain on the fields! May the rivers flow, may the grain grow.

examples.pie: bʰréh₁wr̥ térst. gʷʰéresi ne h₂wérst h₂éǵros-kʷe h₂sowsós. gʷówes péh₂urom h₂mélǵos dédh₃n̥ti. ph₂térm̥ dyḗm gʷr̥néHomes. dyéw nos ph₂ter n̥bʰróm dh₃dʰí. ḱluyéh₁t nos. ḱluyéh₁t wódr̥-kʷe bʰr̥h₁wéni sréwoyh₁t.
examples.en: The well has dried up. It did not rain in the warm weather, and the pasture is dry. The cows give little milk. Let us praise Father Sky. Sky Father, give us rain! May he hear us! May he hear, and may water flow in the well.

examples.pie: nu h₁léwdʰereh₂es h₂ékʷeh₂es sréwete. nu wos ish₁rós h₂n̥gʷʰéys spért. gʷṓs nos h₂ówins-kʷe h₂élete. h₂ékʷeh₂es nos méh₂teres h₁wésuh₂ dh₃té. h₂éǵrons-ge nos wos wédesh₁ pl̥nh₁té. nu-kʷe yúH sweh₂déwih₂es lewkéh₂es-kʷe.
examples.en: Free waters, flow now! Then the strong one freed you from the snake. You nourish our cattle and our sheep. Waters, mothers, give us good things! Fill our fields indeed with your water! And now you are sweet and bright.

examples.pie: kʷíd h₁éyti pótis-kʷe tód ne stoh₂éyeti? tód yóh₁r̥ h₁ésti.
examples.en: What goes, and no ruler makes it stand? It is the year.

examples.pie: tétḱō wiḱpóteyey sédos démet. h₁íd stoh₂éyet. sédos méǵh₂ h₁ést. wéyḱt wiḱpótis h₁íd h₁ésmi-kʷe sédt.
examples.en: The carpenter built a dwelling for the lord. He set it up. The dwelling was great. The lord went into it and sat down in it.

examples.pie: nu h₂épos tn̥nudʰí tód-kʷe stoh₂éye.
examples.en: Now stretch the limb, and make it stand!

examples.pie: kʷésyo swēḱurós só h₁ést? só dh₃trés swēḱurós h₁ést.
examples.en: Whose brother-in-law was he? He was the brother-in-law of the giver.

examples.pie: lémbʰt ḱéh₂dos swēḱuróm só-kʷe séngʷt.
examples.en: Hatred seized the brother-in-law, and he sank.

examples.pie: swēḱurós légʰt spéḱs-kʷe bʰéwdʰt.
examples.en: The brother-in-law lay down, and the watcher woke up.

examples.en: The wolf gave the piglet a pledge: "I will not eat you." The piglet said: "I am confident." Then the wolf broke the pledge and devoured him. If he is hungry, his pledge breaks.

examples.en: Many words, few deeds. The ill-minded man talks; the good man works. Deeds point out the man.

examples.pie: ḱḗr h₁yód wéḱti ǵʰóstos tód dédeh₃ti. dusménesos dóh₃r̥ wisós. péh₂urom ḱéywosyo priHósyo dóh₃r̥ méǵh₂.
examples.en: What the heart wishes, the hand gives. The gift of an ill-minded man is poison. The small gift of a dear friend is great.

examples.pie: péh₂urom péh₂wr̥ méǵh₂m̥ dṓm h₁éwseti. péh₂uros dʰrówgʰos méǵh₂ h₁nómn̥ h₁éwseti. péh₂wr̥ toy h₁éh₃si mē bʰéres.
examples.en: A small fire burns a great house. A small lie burns a great name. Do not carry fire in your mouth.

examples.pie: pótey h₂r̥ǵrós h₁ési dédeh₃si-kʷe nos sh₁esóm.
examples.en: O master, you are shining, and you give us the harvest.

examples.pie: sh₁esós dʰéwgʰt tr̥népt-kʷe me só.

examples.pie: nu ph₃tóm h₂nérm̥ séngʷʰōmes. léymonm̥ péh₃t srowéh₂m-kʷe péh₃t. nu h₂usési h₂ew tr̥syéti. dʰwóri-kʷe h₂énti gʷéHyeti. nu gʷíh₃woyh₁t dʰrā́ks-kʷe h₁ésmōd mē lelikʷyéh₁t.
examples.en: Now let us sing of the drunken man. He drank the lake, and he drank the river. Then at dawn he thirsts again. And he sings in front of the door. Now may he live, and may the dregs not be gone from him!

source.note: ye-present 'bury' from dʰembʰ- 'bury (after cremation)' in the zero grade, LIV²'s present *dʰm̥bʰ-i̯e- continued by Gk θάπτω 'bury' (perf. τέθαμμαι); Arm. damban 'grave' is a noun of the root (Martirosyan 2010, who suspects an Armeno-Greek substratum word). Greek only as a verb, so it is a coinage, not a project reconstruction.
